newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil companies welcome Russia Nemtsov remarks.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil companies welcome Russia Nemtsov remarks.

text.p: TOKYO, June 9 (Reuter) Japanese oil companies, hungry for promises that their terms for giant oil and gas deals in Russia's Sakhalin would hold true, welcomed assurances by Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov on Monday.
"We welcome his statement. We think it's wonderful and take it as a reassurance that our agreements will be honoured," said an official with the semi-governmental Japan National Oil Corp.

Nemtsov told Reuters earlier on Monday that he would work to impose the tax-free conditions to which Japanese and other international companies operating in Sakhalin were entitled under existing production sharing agreements (PSA).

"Now we organise tax-free conditions for Japanese companies who take part in Sakhalin 1 and Sakhalin 2," Nemtsov said, referring to the $22 billion worth of international oil and gas projects in the Sakhalin Island region north of Japan.
Asked whether that meant that he was going to impose the changes during his stay in Japan, Nemtsov simply elaborated on the pledge.
"Free of charge, I mean for exports of machinery, equipment, and so on, for production, in Sakhalin 1 and 2," he said.

"This is good news for the Japanese companies involved in the project and an indication that economic relations are improving between Japan and Russia," said an adviser to one of Japan's most active participants in Sakhalin.

Similar guarantees to Nemtsov's were issued by Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin a year ago, but Japan oil company executives have said that their PSAs were still not being fully honoured by customs and taxation authorities in Sakhalin.
Under the terms of the PSAs, the only taxes the companies should face are profit taxes once oil or gas actually starts flowing, near 2001, according to the latest estimates.
But companies have complained of taxation by regional and local authorities on movements of equipment into the region.
